scope: Bounded source pass for deliberation loop 1. Newton and Tesla are contemporary research lenses on documented practice; no endorsement, participation or invented quotation. Historical passages new relative to the Round31 ledger and the skill references. Patents are proposals; museum custody and USPTO grant are provenance; a search hit is not a verified theorem.

sources.title: 'General Scholium' from the Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy (1729 translation)
sources.author: Isaac Newton (Andrew Motte translation)
sources.version_date: 1729 London edition; Newton Project normalized transcription
sources.section: Page marked <392>: the paragraph 'But hitherto I have not been able to discover the cause of those properties of gravity from phaenomena, and I frame no hypothesis ... In this philosophy particular propositions are inferr'd from the phaenomena, and afterwards render'd general by induction.'
sources.reading_depth: One paragraph read in the normalized English transcription. The Latin drafts A-D (NATP00057-NATP00060) were catalogued only; a search extract renders draft D as 'hypotheses seu mechanicas seu qualitatum occultarum non sequor' and is recorded as an unread extract.
sources.provenance: Primary printed text (posthumous English edition) via the Oxford Newton Project.
sources.claim: Newton distinguishes propositions deduced from phenomena from hypotheses, which he excludes from experimental philosophy.
sources.relevance: Method rule for AV/AX: the interaction-induced coefficient 1/144 must be deduced from the frozen Hamiltonian (I1.5), not posited; induction from finite volumes is replaced by theorem obligations A1-A6.
sources.unresolved_verification: Latin original and drafts not read; translation fidelity not checked against the 1726 Latin edition.

sources.title: Hermes (English translation of the Tabula Smaragdina with Latin commentary), Keynes MS. 28
sources.author: Isaac Newton
sources.version_date: Undated manuscript; Indiana Chymistry of Isaac Newton edition, June 2010
sources.section: Opening translation (summarized) and f. 6v commentary: 'Inferius et superius, fixum et volatile, sulphur et argentum vivum similem habent naturam et sunt una res ut vir et uxor'; 'res omnes id est elementa quatuor ex una hac re quae nostrum Chaos est ... nascuntur'; 'Debet autem prius mundificari separando elementa suaviter et paulatim absque violentia.'
sources.reading_depth: Three Latin sentences of the commentary and a summary of the opening read through extraction; English glosses in the memo are our reconstruction. Full manuscript, facsimile and dating not examined.
sources.provenance: Primary chymical manuscript, King's College Library, Cambridge, via Indiana University scholarly normalized transcription.
sources.claim: Newton glosses the Emerald Tablet's unity of above/below and the gentle separation of elements as chymical doctrine.
sources.relevance: Interpretation only: motivates the exact sector separation of the R-connected excitation cloud from the far vacuum bath (memo Section 5.1) and the two-level energy-ladder check; no unity principle or medium enters the model.
sources.unresolved_verification: Whether the commentary is Newton's own or copied from an authority is not established here; no physical claim is drawn.

sources.title: US 787,412, Art of transmitting electrical energy through the natural mediums
sources.author: Nikola Tesla
sources.section: Specification: three transmission conditions (odd multiple of the quarter wave length; frequency below twenty thousand and not below six per second; wave-train duration not less than one-twelfth or 0.08484 s; mean velocity about 471,240 km/s); claims 1-3.
sources.reading_depth: Selected specification passages and claims 1-3 read from a transcription. Google Patents and freepatentsonline returned HTTP 503 twice; the USPTO scan was not inspected.
sources.provenance: USPTO grant transcribed by a non-archival host; performance statements remain inventor claims.
sources.claim: Proposes stationary electrical waves in the earth under stated numerical resonance and duration conditions.
sources.relevance: A matched duration is a design variable, not a law: the AT4/AW real-time window L is set by the remainder's growth law (first order L*~1/(2k), second order L*~1/(29.3|tau|)); a stated super-luminal mean velocity is recorded as a claim, not adopted.
sources.unresolved_verification: Transcription not compared with the USPTO facsimile; no physical validation of the conditions.

sources.title: US 1,119,732, Apparatus for transmitting electrical energy
sources.author: Nikola Tesla
sources.version_date: Application 1902-01-18 (transcription); a second host lists filing 1907-05-04, consistent with a renewal; granted 1914-12-01
sources.section: Specification passages on the elevated terminal with large radius of curvature, surface density versus limiting pressure without leakage, and 'a terminal of relatively small capacity, which I charge to as high a pressure as practicable'; claims 1-3.
sources.reading_depth: Selected passages and claims read from a transcription; freepatentsonline showed metadata only; Google Patents returned 503. Drawings not inspected.
sources.provenance: USPTO grant via non-archival transcription; metadata cross-checked on a second host.
sources.claim: Proposes preventing leakage at high potential by large-radius conducting boundaries.
sources.relevance: Analogy for summability: the polymer expansion 'leaks' unless a size-weighted anchored norm satisfies the Kotecky-Preiss threshold ln(theta)/13; verified numerically closable at the cap for theta<=7 (memo 5.1, A3).
sources.unresolved_verification: Application/renewal date discrepancy between hosts not resolved against the facsimile.

sources.title: Colorado Springs Notes 1899-1900, page 60 (entry of 1899-07-03)
sources.author: Nikola Tesla (Nikola Tesla Museum edition, commentary by Aleksandar Marincic)
sources.version_date: Manuscript 1899; first published 1978, Nikola Tesla Museum, Belgrade; online transcription
sources.section: Secondary capacity estimate 'Cs = 40 x 1040 cm. approx.', extra coil 1532 cm, total about 2612 cm, inductance 5e7 cm, about 11,800 per second, primary capacity about 0.0717 microfarad (24 jars per side); 'This, of course, gives only an idea and the determination in this manner is far from being exact'; 'Last night the 50,000 volts transformer brought from New York broke down.'
sources.reading_depth: One page read through extraction; adjacent pages and the manuscript facsimile not read.
sources.provenance: Primary laboratory diary held by the Nikola Tesla Museum; the transcription host is not the museum.
sources.claim: Records estimates, a computed frequency, a backward design of primary capacity, an explicit statement of inexactness and an equipment failure.
sources.relevance: Design budgets backwards from a target and retention of failures: memo 5.3-5.4 states the K_2 thresholds (<~1e10 for the cap node; <6.9e5 for the sign of the Wilson mean) and keeps the failed AT4 certificate visible.
sources.unresolved_verification: Numerical values not checked against the printed 1978 edition.

sources.title: The Problem of Increasing Human Energy (Century Magazine, June 1900)
sources.author: Nikola Tesla
sources.section: Formula passage 'the human energy will then be given by the product 1/2 MV^2 = 1/2 MV x V ... V is a certain hypothetical velocity'; section 'ENERGY FROM THE MEDIUM - THE WINDMILL AND THE SOLAR ENGINE - MOTIVE POWER FROM TERRESTRIAL HEAT - ELECTRICITY FROM NATURAL SOURCES' including 'either to turn to use the energy of the sun stored in the ambient medium, or to transmit, through the medium, the sun's energy'.
sources.reading_depth: Two passages read through extraction; the self-acting-engine and wireless sections were not reached (lead). The Round31 skill reference read only the opening analogy.
sources.provenance: Primary published essay via non-archival transcription.
sources.claim: Extends a mechanical energy formula to society with an undefined velocity and proposes deriving energy from the ambient medium.
sources.relevance: Parameter classification rule (no hypothetical variable); the 'medium' motif translated into the odd-in-tau first-order Wilson mean versus the even second-order correlation shift, with the +/-tau mirror control (memo Section 2, table row 6).
sources.unresolved_verification: Century Magazine original not inspected; remaining sections unread.

sources.title: Experiments with Alternate Currents of Very High Frequency and Their Application to Methods of Artificial Illumination (AIEE lecture, Columbia College, 1891-05-20)
sources.author: Nikola Tesla
sources.version_date: Delivered 1891-05-20; reprinted The Electrical World 1891-07-11; online transcription
sources.section: 'alternate current machines capable of giving more than two million reversals of current per minute'; 'with an ordinary coil of, say, 10,000 ohms resistance, the most powerful arc would be produced with about 12,000 alternations per second'; 'the blocks are brought to high degrees of incandescence with much lower potentials than those determined by calculation'; 'the effect is due to the rapidly alternating electrostatic potential ... not to any superimposed vibration'.
sources.reading_depth: Selected sentences read through extraction with approximate positions; the full lecture was not read. The tfcbooks host returned 503.
sources.provenance: Primary lecture text via non-archival transcription.
sources.claim: Reports empirical frequency/potential estimates, discrepancies between calculation and observation, and attribution of an effect to one mechanism.
sources.relevance: Assign each error to its channel and test channels separately: the AT4 three-term split refined to four terms in memo 5.2.
sources.unresolved_verification: Positions approximate; the 1891 Electrical World printing not inspected.

sources.title: Automorphic equivalence within gapped phases of quantum lattice systems
sources.author: Sven Bachmann, Spyridon Michalakis, Bruno Nachtergaele, Robert Sims
sources.version_date: arXiv PDF as served 2026-09-23 (version number not extracted); Commun. Math. Phys. 309 (2012)
sources.section: Assumption 2.2, definition (2.12) of W_gamma, Lemma 2.6 (i)-(iv) with ||W_gamma||_1 <= K/gamma, Remark 2.7 (K ~ 14708), Corollary 2.8 (generator D(s) = int W_gamma(t) e^{itH(s)} H'(s) e^{-itH(s)} dt).
sources.reading_depth: Section 2 lemma statements and remark read from pdftotext extraction of the arXiv PDF; proofs skimmed; the theorem hypotheses for unbounded H(0) noted ('if H(s) is unbounded, this is due to H(0)').
sources.provenance: Primary mathematical paper; extraction of the arXiv PDF.
sources.claim: Spectral flow along a gapped path is generated by a weighted time integral of H'(s); the weight has L1 norm at most K/gamma with K about 14708.
sources.relevance: Route B for observation 1: gives an O(tau) local expectation bound with c_1 ~ (K/gamma)*98 ~ 2.9e6 at gamma=1/2 (delta units), explicit in principle but ~1200x worse than the creation route (memo Section 4, 5.1).
sources.unresolved_verification: Numeric K not recomputed; applicability of Prop. 2.4 to compact-resolvent unbounded on-site terms with bounded V taken as standard but not re-derived.

sources.title: Quasi-locality bounds for quantum lattice systems. Part I. Lieb-Robinson bounds, quasi-local maps, and spectral flow automorphisms
sources.author: Bruno Nachtergaele, Robert Sims, Amanda Young
sources.section: Section 6.2: w_gamma(t)=gamma w(gamma t), (6.34)-(6.36) with ||W_gamma||_1 = (2/gamma) int_0^infty t w(t) dt, (6.39) Fourier property, Corollary 6.6 decay; abstract statement that unbounded on-site Hamiltonians are handled in the strong operator topology.
sources.reading_depth: Abstract and Section 6.2 formulas read from pdftotext extraction; the rest of the 100+ page paper not read.
sources.provenance: Primary review/research paper; arXiv PDF extraction.
sources.claim: Provides a spectral-flow weight with subexponential decay and an L1 norm given by a first moment (not numerically evaluated).
sources.relevance: Alternative weight for route B; its constant is a coder task (memo Section 7).
sources.unresolved_verification: First moment of w not evaluated; strong-topology spectral flow hypotheses not matched to the AQ model.

sources.title: On the dynamics of lattice systems with unbounded on-site terms in the Hamiltonian
sources.author: Bruno Nachtergaele, Robert Sims
sources.section: Abstract: supplies the arguments completing proofs of Lieb-Robinson bounds and the thermodynamic limit of the dynamics for unbounded on-site terms.
sources.reading_depth: Abstract only (the AQ1 report cites its Section 3/Theorem 4.1; not re-read here).
sources.claim: Lieb-Robinson bounds and infinite-volume dynamics hold with unbounded on-site terms and bounded interactions.
sources.relevance: Premise for the far-star tail in route B and for AQ1's dynamics; not needed for route A.
sources.unresolved_verification: Theorem statements and constants not re-read.

sources.title: Ground states in relatively bounded quantum perturbations of classical lattice systems
sources.author: D. A. Yarotsky
sources.section: Abstract: gap, exponential decay of truncated correlations, analyticity of the ground state; AKLT application.
sources.claim: General perturbation theory for relatively bounded quantum perturbations of classical lattice systems with existential constants.
sources.relevance: The framework AM2 replaces with explicit constants; its c1/c2 remain unevaluated in the project.
sources.unresolved_verification: Hypotheses not matched to Casimir on-site terms.

sources.title: Expansions for one quasiparticle states in spin 1/2 systems
sources.author: Nilanjana Datta, Tom Kennedy
sources.section: Abstract: convergent expansions of ground and low-lying excited wavefunctions for quantum transverse Ising; convergent single-quasiparticle dispersion.
sources.reading_depth: Abstract only; the Kirkwood-Thomas form of the expansion and volume uniformity not verified from the body.
sources.claim: Convergent ground-state expansions exist for spin-1/2 perturbed lattice systems.
sources.relevance: Model for 'local expectations analytic in the coupling'; finite-dimensional sites, not directly applicable.

sources.title: Lie-Schwinger block-diagonalization and gapped quantum chains with unbounded interactions
sources.author: S. Del Vecchio, J. Froehlich, A. Pizzo, S. Rossi
sources.section: Abstract: chains; interactions form-bounded with respect to on-site terms; gap uniform in chain length for small coupling.
sources.claim: Uniform gap for one-dimensional chains with unbounded, form-bounded interactions at small coupling.
sources.relevance: Nearest published setting to AM2 (unbounded on-site); one-dimensional and existential; AM2's explicit finite-volume constants are complementary.
sources.unresolved_verification: Smallness threshold and method details not read.

sources.title: Block-diagonalization of infinite-volume lattice Hamiltonians with unbounded interactions
sources.author: Simone Del Vecchio, Juerg Froehlich, Alessandro Pizzo
sources.version_date: arXiv v1 2021-08-31; a Journal of Functional Analysis listing was seen in search and not verified
sources.section: Abstract: arbitrary dimension; on-site gapped terms plus relatively bounded short-range interactions times coupling t; gap strictly positive for |t| small independent of lattice size.
sources.claim: Uniform gap in arbitrary dimension for relatively bounded unbounded interactions at small coupling; no explicit constants.
sources.relevance: Closest higher-dimensional analogue of AM2; existential threshold; not usable numerically at the cap.

sources.title: Persistence of exponential decay and spectral gaps for interacting fermions
sources.author: Wojciech De Roeck, Manfred Salmhofer
sources.section: Abstract: weakly interacting lattice fermions, gapped free system, convergent fermionic perturbation theory, gap uniform in lattice size, non-self-adjoint interactions allowed.
sources.claim: Gap persistence for weakly interacting fermions via convergent perturbation theory; existential smallness.
sources.relevance: Perturbative-uniformity precedent; fermionic, not applicable to SU(2) links.

sources.title: Enhanced Lieb-Robinson bounds for commuting long-range interactions
sources.author: Marius Lemm, Tom Wessel
sources.section: Abstract: enhanced LRB t r^{-alpha} for commuting long-range interactions; enhanced ground-state correlation bounds and an enhanced local-perturbations-perturb-locally principle.
sources.claim: LPPL and correlation enhancements for commuting interactions.
sources.relevance: Whole-star interactions do not commute; lead only for any future commuting-subfamily control.

sources.title: The bulk spectral gap is semi-decidable: a convergent family of certified upper bounds
sources.author: Xiangling Xu, Matthias Schoetz, Jie Wang, Victor Magron, Igor Klep, Omar Fawzi, Marc-Olivier Renou
sources.section: Abstract: SDP hierarchy of certified upper bounds on the bulk gap; application to the kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet.
sources.claim: Certified upper bounds on bulk gaps converge; semi-decidability.
sources.relevance: Potential independent tool for the AZ finite graph (finite-dimensional sites after cutoff); upper bounds only, never a gap lower bound.
sources.unresolved_verification: Not peer reviewed as far as seen; hypotheses unread.

sources.title: A Constructive Proof of Existence and Mass Gap for Pure SU(3) Yang-Mills in Four-Dimensional Space-Time
sources.author: D. C. Jacobsen
sources.section: Abstract page and arXiv admin note: 'This submission has been withdrawn because it does not meet arXiv's research content quality standards'.
sources.claim: Claims a complete constructive proof of existence and mass gap for SU(3) on R^4.
sources.relevance: Recorded as a claimed solution and as discourse; no content is used.

sources.title: Towards a Proof of Mass Gap in 3d Yang-Mills Theory
sources.author: V. P. Nair
sources.section: Abstract: 'We give the outlines of a proof for the existence of a mass gap for the 3d Yang-Mills theory in terms of an inequality on the eigenvalues of the Laplacian on the gauge-invariant configuration space.'
sources.claim: An outline, not a theorem, for a 3d mass gap.
sources.relevance: Distinguished from a 4d theorem; no premise imported.
sources.unresolved_verification: Body unread; status of the inequality unknown.
